correctness.rationale: PASS: for n>=3 the 1-skeleton of the second hypersimplex Δ(n,2) is J(n,2), and each Johnson edge belongs to a unique triangle indexed by a triple i,j,k. Generic hyperplane signs of e_i+e_j are threshold-graph edges (weights a_i+a_j-t); every mixed sign triple contributes exactly two crossing Johnson edges, so f_0=2M(G). In a creation ordering of threshold graph, pair signs on i<j<k are b_j,b_k,b_k, thus M(G)=sum_{i=1}^{n-2}Z_iO_i over suffix zeros/ones. Each term <=floor((n-i)^2/4) with equality exactly when all suffixes are balanced. Existence of each threshold construction as strict additive weights gives generic equality realizability. For centered hyperplanes a_i=i-(n+1)/2 with arbitrarily small centered generic perturbation, triples counted via strict mixed pair sums and complementary tie pairs total the same maximal M; construction works all n. Nongeneric sections cannot exceed generic by an inward/parallel perturbation of section vertices, consistent with De Loera–Lopez-Campos–Torres Lemma 2.1. Elementary sum equals binom(n,3)+floor((n-1)^2/4). Independently enumerated all 1020 threshold words for n=3..10, verifying mixed triples, equality words and maxima; finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

evidence: De Loera–Lopez-Campos–Torres, Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 2.1, bounds vertices of cuts in arbitrary polytopes and gives generic perturbation, with no Δ(n,2) sharp specialization; Kaibel–Walter focuses polytope extension complexity/adjacency.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Putting N=binom(n,2) into general O(N^2) bound yields O(n^4), not the exact smaller O(n^3) number. The generic perturbation lemma is appropriately credited, but general theorem does not imply the coefficient or balanced-suffix equality classification.
